Sam — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call with the HelioHealth engineering team and the follow-ups we discussed: 

- SLO targets you called out: p95 latency <= 150ms for streaming responses (interactive), sustained throughput ~200 req/s, concurrency spikes up to 50 concurrent users, and ability to stream partial tokens with <50ms token step latency.
- Typical prompt distribution: 70% short prompts (~40 tokens), 25% medium (~180 tokens), 5% long (up to 1,200 tokens). Average generated tokens per request ~120.
- Compliance note: HIPAA-sensitive PHI; we'll treat this as private deployment considerations for audit/logging and key management (we'll surface options in the perf plan).

Next steps we agreed on:
1) You to share a lightweight workload profile (attached is the CSV format).
2) Redwood to run a short perf validation: 1) baseline latency numbers across candidate model variants, 2) quantify throughput with continuous batching and prefix caching, and 3) run a streaming token step latency check. Estimated turnaround: 3 business days after we get the workload CSV + temporary test credentials.
3) We'll provide a short cost estimate for hitting the SLO using cost levers (batching, caching, quantization) and two rollout options (canary -> full, or staged region rollouts).

I've attached the CSV template (helio_workload_profile.csv). If the Helio team can return it today/tomorrow we can kick off perf tests by end of week.

Thanks for the workload file, Sam — this is exactly what we need to scope an initial perf run. High-level plan attached (redwood_perf_plan.pdf). A brief technical summary of how we'd approach your targets and the cost/performance levers we recommend: 

1) Baseline model variants to test
   - small/medium open variants (fast, cheap) for low-latency short prompts
   - larger instruction-tuned models for high-quality long responses
   - a quantized medium model (INT8 or 4-bit) as a potential sweet spot for p95 latency/cost

2) Latency & streaming strategy
   - Continuous batching: keep a small batching window (~5–10ms) for peak throughput to reduce per-token compute cost without significantly increasing tail latency.
   - Prefix/KV caching: for repeated prompt prefixes (clinical templates), use KV cache to cut compute for warm paths — can reduce p95 by ~20–40% for those flows.
   - Streaming optimization: prioritize immediate token emission (lower N-gram post-processing) and measure token-step latency; we aim for token-step <50ms on tested hardware.

3) Throughput/concurrency handling
   - Autoscaling pools with prewarmed instances for expected spike windows (shift changes).
   - Configure concurrency soft limits per instance and route excess to warm standby nodes to avoid cold-start latency.

4) Quantization & model selection tradeoffs
   - INT8/4-bit quantization can reduce memory and increase throughput (2–3x improvement) at modest quality degradation on many tasks; we'll run QAed evals on your eval prompts.
   - If quantization impacts clinical-relevant outputs, we recommend hybrid approach: quantized runner for short/template flows and FP16 for high-risk/long responses.

5) Cost estimate approach
   - We'll produce a per-1k-req cost estimate under two configs: (A) prioritized latency (p95 <=150ms) using smaller specialized variants + batching + caching; (B) balanced quality/cost with quantized medium model and staged rollout.

Action items for HelioHealth: provide temporary sandbox creds (S3 bucket or test VPC) and confirm a 2-hour window for our perf run. We can start as early as today if you confirm.
